svg.title: A DAY AT THE HUB
svg.desc: A day at a new bus yard with no grid connection: chargers and AXIVAI battery storage are installed, but the utility transformer is on back order and its pad stands empty. An AXIVAI Mothership, an electric truck with a battery trailer, fills up at an energy terminal, drives to the yard and backs into the AXIVAI dock, where it unloads into the storage. Overnight the storage charges every bus while a second truck tops it up. In the morning every bus leaves full and the next truck is already filling. Energy figures are AXIVAI estimates for a 40-bus yard: about 4 MWh a night, two 2 MWh deliveries.
svg.text: A new bus yard with no grid connection, powered by AXIVAI.

g.text: Estimate · ~100 kWh per bus; 2 MWh per trailer
The wait: a new yard with chargers and buses, but no grid connection.
Power on wheels: AXIVAI trucks deliver energy into storage on the yard.
Overnight: the storage charges every bus; a second truck tops it up.
Morning: every bus leaves full, with power still in reserve.
Estimate · ~100 kWh per bus; 2 MWh per trailer
A new bus yard. The chargers are installed and the buses are here, but there is no power: the
utility transformer the yard needs is on back order.
PG&E EV sites: 560 days to power (2026)
An AXIVAI Mothership fills up at an energy terminal, drives onto the yard and backs into the
AXIVAI dock. Its load charges the storage installed on the yard.
About 4 MWh of storage on the yard
Overnight, the storage charges every bus, with no grid connection. A second truck arrives during
the night and tops the storage back up.
About 100 kWh per bus per night
2 deliveries a day for a 40-bus yard
Morning. Every bus leaves full and the next truck is already filling up. When the transformer
arrives, the storage can stay on as backup.

svg.text: Figures marked Estimate are AXIVAI planning figures.
Time to power: PG&E biannual energization report to the CPUC, Rule 29 EV projects, end-to-end average (April 2026). NY upgrade dates: NYSEG and RG&E petition to the PSC (November
2024). Energy figures: AXIVAI estimates for a 40-bus yard, about 100 kWh per bus per night and 2 MWh per trailer.
